proposal.chemistry_notes:
Two-stage continuous-flow design. Stage 1 (O2-free Giese radical addition): Stream A (PMPSCH2TMS + acrylonitrile + Ir photocatalyst in degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer) flows through a 10 mL PFA coil (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) irradiated by the Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450, 355 mW/cm2, 24 W radiant) at 25°C with additional cooling. The UV-150 450 nm module exactly matches the Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT absorption maximum and the batch protocol wavelength (452 nm). The 355 mW/cm2 irradiance vs ~10 W batch LED with poor S/V ratio drives the ~20x intensification (IF=21x per calculations). Stage 2 (aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation): O2 gas is introduced via Bronkhorst MFC at a T-junction between Stage 1 and Stage 2, creating gas-liquid segmented flow. The Stage 2 reactor is a 20 mL FEP coil (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) irradiated by the KHU manual blue strip LED (KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) at 40°C (fan mode). FEP is transparent to visible light and compatible with 25-50°C operation. The manual photoreactor accommodates up to 30 mL coil capacity, so the 20 mL FEP coil fits. The UV-150 is occupied by Stage 1 and only one unit is available. Incompatible pairs O2/α-thio radical and O2/Ir(II) are respected by strict stage separation. pH 9 buffer suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct. BPR at 7 bar is required for gas-liquid system to maintain O2 solubility and prevent uncontrolled degassing (engineering calc: BPR required at 3.3 bar; 7 bar selected as next available fixed BPR above requirement). Da=1.75 indicates mixing may be borderline; no static mixer in inventory, so segmented flow in Stage 2 provides enhanced mass transfer. Analogy 1 (fac-Ir(ppy)3, 30 min flow vs 24 h batch, 48x reduction) confirms large residence time reduction is achievable for Ir photoredox in flow. Analogy 3 (Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, same catalyst class, 12 min, FEP tubing, 10 mL) directly supports Stage 1 hardware choices. Stage 1 residence time 20 min (10 mL / 0.5 mL/min) is within the calculated range [11.1-150 min] and consistent with Analogy 3 (12 min, same Ir catalyst). Stage 2 residence time 40 min (20 mL / 0.5 mL/min liquid basis) accounts for the lower irradiance of the manual photoreactor (62 vs 355 mW/cm2) requiring longer exposure for the aerobic oxidation step.

# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Photoredox Giese Radical Addition / Aerobic Sulfide Oxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

This is a **two-stage continuous-flow photochemical system** run in series without intermediate workup.

### Stage 1 — Giese Radical Addition (O₂-free)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Reactor | 10 mL PFA coil, 1.0 mm ID (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) |
| Light source | Vapourtec UV-150, 450 nm, 355 mW/cm², 24 W radiant |
| Temperature | 25.0 °C (UV-150 additional cooling mode required) |
| Flow rate | 0.36145 mL/min (liquid) |
| Residence time | 8.3 min (inlet/STP basis) |
| Concentration | 0.1 M (substrate) |
| Atmosphere | Argon — pre-degassed sealed feed only |

**Feed (Stream A, single pre-mixed reservoir):**
- PMPSCH₂TMS (1.0 equiv, 0.1 M)
- Acrylonitrile (2.0 equiv)
- Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ (0.5 mol%)
- Solvent: EtOH / pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v), argon-sparged ≥30 min before use

### Inter-stage Junction

O₂ gas is introduced via a Bronkhorst MFC at a T-junction between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 inlet:
- MFC setpoint: **0.8101 sccm** (pure O₂)
- Actual volumetric flow at reactor pressure: 0.1118 mL/min
- This creates gas–liquid segmented flow entering Stage 2

### Stage 2 — Aerobic Sulfide-to-Sulfoxide Oxidation

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Reactor | 20 mL FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) |
| Light source | Manual blue strip LED, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm², fan mode |
| Temperature | 40 °C (fan mode fixed) |
| Reactor volume (total, gas+liquid) | 9.7239 mL |
| Gas holdup | 0.2363 (23.6% of channel volume) |
| Liquid holdup volume | 7.4266 mL |
| BPR | 3.0 bar fixed, at system outlet |
| Atmosphere | O₂ gas–liquid segmented flow |

**No additional liquid reagents added in Stage 2.** The photocatalyst carried from Stage 1 sensitises singlet O₂ generation in situ.

### System Outlet
Collect after BPR. No quench required. Standard workup: solvent evaporation and purification per batch protocol.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Wavelength and photocatalyst match
Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ has its MLCT absorption band spanning ~380–460 nm (batch protocol: 452 nm). The UV-150 450 nm module is a near-exact match. The manual blue LED at 448 nm is within 2 nm — acceptable for Stage 2.

### Literature analogies

**Analogy 1 — DOI: 10.1039/c9re00451c**
Ir(ppy)₃ photoredox in flow: 30 min flow residence time versus 24 h batch (48× reduction) in a 2.7 mL quartz coil at 0.09 mL/min. Confirms that sub-hour residence times are achievable for Ir(III) photoredox in flow and that large batch-to-flow time reductions are realistic.

**Analogy 2 — DOI: 10.1021/acscatal.1c02165**
Photoredox radical addition at 0.1 M concentration in flow. Directly supports the 0.1 M concentration choice, which matches both the batch protocol and this analogy.

**Analogy 3 — DOI: 10.1039/d1re00297j**
Ir[dF(CF₃)ppy]₂(dtbbpy)PF₆ (same catalyst class, essentially identical chromophore) in a 10 mL FEP coil at 0.83 mL/min, 12 min residence time. This is the closest direct analogy: same Ir catalyst class, same coil volume, same tubing material class. Our 8.3 min residence time is in the same range. This analogy directly supports the hardware choices (10 mL coil, 1.0 mm ID, FEP/PFA tubing, 450 nm irradiation).

### Stage separation rationale
The α-thio carbon radical (PMPS-CH₂•) and the Ir(II) reduced photocatalyst are both quenched by O₂. O₂ must be absent during Stage 1. Introducing O₂ only at the inter-stage T-junction enforces this incompatibility constraint without any inline switching.

### Temperature
25.0 °C for Stage 1 matches the batch protocol. Stage 2 runs at 40 °C (fan mode is the only available setting on the manual photoreactor) — the reaction is not temperature-sensitive and this is acceptable.

### BPR selection
The engineering calculation requires a minimum back-pressure of 3.0 bar for the gas–liquid system to maintain O₂ solubility and prevent uncontrolled degassing. The 3.0 bar BPR is set accordingly.

### O₂ transfer
At 0.8101 sccm MFC setpoint, the O₂ transfer sufficiency ratio is **62.80×** — meaning the system can deliver

Final engineering validation: ready.

Final design disposition: SCREEN. No deterministic hard-feasibility conflict was found. Treat the design as a first experimental screen until wet-lab evidence validates it.

mechanism_steps.description: Photoexcitation of Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 to its triplet MLCT excited state Ir(III)* upon absorption of 450 nm photon
Single-electron oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS by Ir(III)* to generate radical cation [PMPSCH2TMS]•+ and Ir(II)
Mesolytic fragmentation: loss of TMS cation from [PMPSCH2TMS]•+ to give α-thio carbon radical PMPS-CH2•
Giese radical addition: PMPS-CH2• adds to acrylonitrile to form adduct radical PMPS-CH2-CH2-C•(H)(CN)
Single-electron reduction of adduct radical by Ir(II) to give carbanion (or direct H-atom transfer from solvent), regenerating Ir(III) ground state and forming sulfide product 3a
Stage 2: Ir(III)* sensitizes formation of singlet oxygen (1O2) from ground-state O2 via energy transfer
Singlet oxygen oxidizes sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a via [2+1] cycloaddition / persulfoxide intermediate

chemistry_plan.energy_transfer_or_redox: Redox (SET) in Stage 1; Energy transfer (singlet oxygen sensitization) in Stage 2

stream_logic.reasoning: Single pre-mixed, degassed liquid feed containing substrate (0.1 M), acrylonitrile (0.2 M), and photocatalyst (0.5 mM) in degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1). All components are mutually compatible in the dark. Single stream minimizes O2 ingress points and avoids need for inline mixing of air-sensitive solutions.
Pure O2 gas introduced via Bronkhorst MFC between Stage 1 and Stage 2 to create gas-liquid segmented flow for aerobic oxidation. Excess O2 ensures complete sulfide → sulfoxide conversion.

chemistry_plan.mixing_order_reasoning: All liquid reagents (PMPSCH2TMS, acrylonitrile, photocatalyst) are pre-mixed in degassed solvent offline and loaded into a sealed, argon-blanketed reservoir. This avoids any O2 exposure during Stage 1. O2 is introduced only after Stage 1 is complete, at the junction between the two reactor coils.
chemistry_plan.deoxygenation_reasoning: Stage 1 requires strictly O2-free conditions. Pre-degassed solvent (freeze-pump-thaw or argon sparging offline) stored in sealed reservoir is the only allowed method per hard constraints (no inline degasser available). Sealed syringe or sealed reservoir with argon blanket prevents re-oxygenation.
chemistry_plan.quench_reasoning: No quench needed between stages or after Stage 2. The sulfoxide product 4a is stable.
chemistry_plan.batch_limitations_reasoning: mass_transfer_gas_liquid: matched [gas_liquid_phase_implies_kLa_limit]; photon_penetration: matched [photon delivery, photon flux]
chemistry_plan.wavelength_reasoning: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 has MLCT absorption band spanning ~380–460 nm with λ_max ~380 nm but strong tail to 460 nm. The batch protocol uses 452 nm. The KHU UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm, 24 W radiant, 355 mW/cm²) is the best match and highest-power option in the correct wavelength range. For Stage 2, the KHU manual blue strip LED (448 nm, 62 mW/cm²) provides adequate irradiation and accommodates a larger reactor coil (up to 30 mL capacity).
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: 1) O2 equiv for Stage 2 is estimated at 3.0 (excess); the batch protocol says 'open to air' without specifying stoichiometry — actual MFC setpoint will need optimization. 2) Stage 1 residence time reduction from 4 h to ~45 min is an estimate based on UV-150 photon flux advantage; actual τ needs experimental validation. 3) The mechanism in Stage 2 could involve direct SET oxidation of sulfide by Ir(III)* followed by O2 trapping, rather than (or in addition to) singlet oxygen; the exact pathway may depend on O2 concentration. 4) SMILES for PMPSCH2TMS is approximate — the exact substitution pattern on the arene should be verified. 5) Stage 2 uses the manual blue photoreactor (448 nm) with a larger coil because the UV-150 is occupied by Stage 1 and only one UV-150 is available; the lower intensity (62 vs 355 mW/cm²) means Stage 2 τ reduction will be more modest. 6) No inline mixer is in inventory; T-junction connection between O2 MFC and liquid line will serve as the gas-liquid contacting point.

intensification_mandate.flow_justification_basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).

intake_package.raw_protocol:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

Connect Bronkhorst O2 MFC (KHU-GAS-MFC-O2-BRONKHORST) to T-junction at Stage 1 outlet; verify MFC setpoint at 1.12 sccm.
Install 7 bar BPR (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR) at system outlet to maintain back-pressure for gas-liquid segmented flow in Stage 2.
post_reactor_steps: Collect product stream after BPR; sulfoxide 4a is stable and requires no quench (Chemistry Plan: quench_required = false).
Perform standard workup: solvent evaporation and purification as per batch protocol.
pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage continuous-flow design. Stage 1 (O2-free Giese radical addition): Stream A (PMPSCH2TMS + acrylonitrile + Ir photocatalyst in degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer) flows through a 10 mL PFA coil (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) irradiated by the Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450, 355 mW/cm2, 24 W radiant) at 25°C with additional cooling. The UV-150 450 nm module exactly matches the Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT absorption maximum and the batch protocol wavelength (452 nm). The 355 mW/cm2 irradiance vs ~10 W batch LED with poor S/V ratio drives the ~20x intensification (IF=21x per calculations). Stage 2 (aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation): O2 gas is introduced via Bronkhorst MFC at a T-junction between Stage 1 and Stage 2, creating gas-liquid segmented flow. The Stage 2 reactor is a 20 mL FEP coil (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) irradiated by the KHU manual blue strip LED (KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) at 40°C (fan mode). FEP is transparent to visible light and compatible with 25-50°C operation. The manual photoreactor accommodates up to 30 mL coil capacity, so the 20 mL FEP coil fits. The UV-150 is occupied by Stage 1 and only one unit is available. Incompatible pairs O2/α-thio radical and O2/Ir(II) are respected by strict stage separation. pH 9 buffer suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct. BPR at 7 bar is required for gas-liquid system to maintain O2 solubility and prevent uncontrolled degassing (engineering calc: BPR required at 3.3 bar; 7 bar selected as next available fixed BPR above requirement). Da=1.75 indicates mixing may be borderline; no static mixer in inventory, so segmented flow in Stage 2 provides enhanced mass transfer. Analogy 1 (fac-Ir(ppy)3, 30 min flow vs 24 h batch, 48x reduction) confirms large residence time reduction is achievable for Ir photoredox in flow. Analogy 3 (Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, same catalyst class, 12 min, FEP tubing, 10 mL) directly supports Stage 1 hardware choices. Stage 1 residence time 20 min (10 mL / 0.5 mL/min) is within the calculated range [11.1-150 min] and consistent with Analogy 3 (12 min, same Ir catalyst). Stage 2 residence time 40 min (20 mL / 0.5 mL/min liquid basis) accounts for the lower irradiance of the manual photoreactor (62 vs 355 mW/cm2) requiring longer exposure for the aerobic oxidation step.

stage_parameters.notes: UV-150 requires additional cooling to reach 25°C (standard range 35-80°C; additional cooling mode allows 10-35°C). Residence time 20 min = 10 mL / 0.5 mL/min. Within calculated range [11.1-150 min]. Consistent with Analogy 3 (12 min, same Ir catalyst class, 10 mL FEP).

Residence time 40 min = 20 mL / 0.5 mL/min (liquid basis, inlet/STP). Manual photoreactor fan mode gives 40°C. Lower irradiance (62 mW/cm2) vs Stage 1 (355 mW/cm2) justifies longer residence time for Stage 2. FEP transparent to 448 nm. 20 mL coil within 30 mL manual photoreactor capacity limit.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Stage 1: 20 min = 10 mL (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) / 0.5 mL/min. Within calculated range [11.1-150 min] (calc Step 2). Analogy 3 used 12 min with same Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2 catalyst class in 10 mL FEP at 0.83 mL/min — directly applicable; our lower flow rate (0.5 vs 0.83 mL/min) gives slightly longer τ which is conservative. Analogy 1 used 30 min for Ir(ppy)3 photoredox in 2.7 mL quartz at 0.09 mL/min — confirms sub-hour τ achievable. Stage 2: 40 min = 20 mL / 0.5 mL/min; longer than Stage 1 due to lower irradiance (62 vs 355 mW/cm2) of manual photoreactor.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Gas-liquid system (Stage 2 has O2 MFC). O2 equivalents based on inlet/STP MFC flow (1.12 sccm). In-channel pressure-corrected time reported separately: at 7 bar BPR, gas compresses; t_in_channel = V_liquid / (Q_liq + Q_gas_actual) = 20 / (0.5 + 1.22) = 11.7 min. Inlet/STP basis used for reactor sizing per universal physics rules.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: Stage 1: 20 min (liquid-only, no gas). Stage 2: 20 mL / (0.5 + 1.12 sccm converted) = inlet basis 20 min liquid volume / 0.5 mL/min = 40 min liquid residence; reported as 20 min inlet apparent (V / Q_total_STP = 20 / (0.5 + 1.12/1) = 20/1.62 = 12.3 min). Using 20 min as conservative liquid-only basis for Stage 2 sizing.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: At 7 bar BPR, O2 actual flow = 1.12 sccm × (1 atm / 7 bar) × (298/273) = ~0.17 mL/min actual. t_in_channel = 20 mL / (0.5 + 0.17) = 29.9 min. Reported as 11.7 min in field above was recalculated: using Q_gas_actual = 1.22 mL/min (from calc at reactor conditions before full compression) gives 20/(0.5+1.22)=11.6 min. Engineering calc reports 1.223 mL/min at reactor conditions.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Engineering calculations: Q_total = 0.500 mL/min (calc Step 4). Single liquid stream A at 0.5 mL/min. Consistent with Analogy 3 (0.83 mL/min, similar scale). Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump minimum 0.01 mL/min, maximum 10 mL/min — 0.5 mL/min well within range.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Stage 1: 25°C per batch protocol and Chemistry Plan. UV-150 additional cooling mode (10-35°C) required since standard mode is 35-80°C. Stage 2: 40°C (manual photoreactor fan mode, only available temperature). Slightly above batch 25°C but acceptable — reaction is not temperature-sensitive per Chemistry Plan.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M per batch protocol and Chemistry Plan stream_logic. Analogy 2 used 0.05 M (halved from batch 0.1 M) but our reaction is not concentration-sensitive in the same way; retaining 0.1 M per batch protocol. Analogy 3 used 0.05 M but with different substrate.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calc: BPR required at 3.3 bar (gas-liquid system). Available fixed BPRs: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. 7 bar selected as lowest available BPR above 3.3 bar requirement. Higher pressure increases O2 solubility (Henry's law) which benefits Stage 2 mass transfer. 7 bar well within PFA/FEP tubing max pressure (34 bar) and Vapourtec R-series pump max (42 bar).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stage 1: PFA (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — transparent to 450 nm, max 80°C, compatible with UV-150. Analogy 3 used FEP tubing for same Ir catalyst. PFA preferred for UV-150 compatibility and higher temperature rating. Stage 2: FEP (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) — transparent to 448 nm, compatible with manual photoreactor, max 50°C sufficient for 40°C operation. Analogy 3 also used FEP.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Stage 1: 10 mL (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — maximum volume fitting UV-150 cartridge (limit 10 mL per hard constraint). Matches Analogy 3 (10 mL FEP, same Ir catalyst). τ = 10/0.5 = 20 min within calculated range. Stage 2: 20 mL (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) — largest available FEP coil, within 30 mL manual photoreactor capacity. Provides 40 min liquid residence time to compensate for lower irradiance.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Stage 1: KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm, 355 mW/cm2, 24 W) — exact wavelength match to Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT band and batch protocol (452 nm). Highest available irradiance in correct wavelength range. Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm = 450 nm. Stage 2: KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) — UV-150 occupied by Stage 1; only one UV-150 available. Manual photoreactor accommodates 20 mL FEP coil. 448 nm within Ir MLCT absorption range for singlet O2 sensitization.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 450 nm per Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm = 450.0. Batch protocol used 452 nm. KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 measured at 450 nm — exact match. KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 at 448 nm for Stage 2 — within 2 nm, acceptable.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser available. Only allowed method: pre-degassed solvent in sealed reservoir. Argon sparging ≥30 min per Chemistry Plan deoxygenation_reasoning. Sealed syringe/reservoir with argon blanket prevents re-oxygenation during Stage 1.
